prompt:
## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Hive Scale
where: ScaleRepository (uses), src/persistence/repositories.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly items = new Map<string, ScaleRecord>();
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:
- class ScaleRepository (node 18ab235f6c31a91a): layer infrastructure, component persistence, fan-out 0, fan-in 5
- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.linkScale
- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.listScales
- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.recordReading
- <- CALLS Method ScaleService.sendAlert
- <- CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS Class ScaleService

### B
concept: Hive
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const hive = this.hives.findById(hiveId);
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:
- class TreatmentService (node 2912145e8ad12343): layer domain, component business, fan-out 12, fan-in 0
- -> CALLS Method HarvestRepository.create

- -> CALLS Method HiveRepository.findById

response.rationale: These are two different concepts. A is a hive scale, a weighing device. ScaleRepository stores ScaleRecord items ("private readonly items = new Map<string, ScaleRecord>();"), and ScaleService uses it to link scales, record readings and send alerts. B is the hive itself, the colony the business revolves around. TreatmentService looks it up through HiveRepository.findById ("const hive = this.hives.findById(hiveId);"). A scale can be attached to a hive and send readings about it, but it is a separate thing with its own repository and service, so the two are related, not the same.
